Hi finance team / Laura,

Following up on Arcadia’s recent pilot close — they were granted a $25k trial stipend as part of the PO. Arcadia has asked us to apply the stipend against Invoice #9934 rather than receive a standalone credit memo. I’ve attached the invoice and the signed promo agreement for reference.

Questions we need answered to move forward:
- Do we emit a credit memo referencing Invoice 9934 (apply as invoice offset), or do we post a contra-revenue adjustment to the GLA and leave their invoice untouched?
- If credit memo, which AR / GLA should be used for bookkeeping (promo allowance vs contra-revenue account)?
- Any tax implications our tax team flags for invoice-offset treatment vs separate credit?

Arcadia (Maya) prefers the invoice offset because it simplifies their reconciliation. If finance is OK with offset, they’ve agreed to sign an acknowledgement (DocuSign) — link in the Drive.

Can we get a recommended accounting path and required journals so I can confirm with Arcadia?

Chloe / Marcus / Karthik,

Finance view below — high level recommendation and required actions.

Recommendation: issue an internal credit memo that references Invoice 9934 and apply it as an invoice offset. Rationale: the stipend was promotional consideration tied directly to the pilot; treating as contra-revenue complicates downstream revenue reporting and customer reconciliation.

Required bookkeeping steps (summary):
- Create Credit Memo CM-2025-078 referencing Invoice 9934 (customer-facing).
- AR: apply CM-2025-078 to Invoice 9934 to net the outstanding balance.
- GL posting: Debit Promo Allowance (G/L 6402) $25,000; Credit Accounts Receivable (G/L 1101) $25,000.
- Revenue team to record any necessary reversing entries at month-end if recognition is impacted.

Tax note: tax needs to confirm treatment for promo allowances; I’ll loop in tax for signoff but historically we post to Promo Allowance.

Attachments: please send the signed acknowledgement to finance@redwood.com once Arcadia signs.

Laura Bennett
